findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Basic.lean:67 `smul_left : B (a • x) y = a * B x y`, :71 `smul_right : B x (a • y) = a * B x y`; TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean:132-134 `@[simp] integralForm_cast : (L.integralForm x y : ℚ) = L.form x y`. The proof itself is just those three rewrites plus `ring`.
findings.fix: Delete `form_smul_smul` and its doc bullet; any such goal closes with `simp [LinearMap.BilinForm.smul_left, LinearMap.BilinForm.smul_right]` then `ring`.
findings.issue: `form_smul_smul` is a composite of `LinearMap.BilinForm.smul_left`/`smul_right` and the existing `@[simp] integralForm_cast`; it has no consumer in the repo (grep `form_smul_smul` matches only its own definition and the module-doc bullet at line 34).

findings.evidence: Rationalization.lean:68-71 `@[simp] rationalizationEquiv_tmul : L.rationalizationEquiv (q ⊗ₜ x) = q • (x : V)`; lines 74-76 prove the `1 ⊗ₜ` case by `simp`. Mathlib likewise keeps only `IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul` (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/IsTensorProduct.lean:416) with no `equiv_one_tmul` variant.
findings.fix: Delete `rationalizationEquiv_one_tmul` and its doc entry; use `rationalizationEquiv_tmul` (simp discharges the `1 • x` step).
findings.issue: `rationalizationEquiv_one_tmul` is the `q = 1` special case of `rationalizationEquiv_tmul` (same file, line 68, `@[simp]`) composed with `one_smul`; its proof is literally `simp`, and nothing uses it.

summary: The base-change lemma, the lattice `isBaseChange_subtype`, and the rationalization equiv/isometry are new and reuse Mathlib's canonical `IsBaseChange`, `BilinForm.baseChange`, and `Basis.extendOfIsLattice` correctly. Two lemmas are pure restatements of existing simp lemmas: `form_smul_smul` (relocated from the previous round, not removed) and `rationalizationEquiv_one_tmul`.
